names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 3 martie, «Sfântul Mucenic Vasilisc».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 3 Μαρτίου, «Άγιοι Ευτρόπιος, Κλεόνικος και Βασιλίσκος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 3 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученици Евтропије, Клеоник и Василиск.“, which names three men; this man's own name is taken out of it, with the rank word мученици left off and Свети, which is not a rank. The heading gives no epithet and does not name Amasea, which this folder's English name carries from the other calendars.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 3 марта ст. ст., name page 391, «Мученик Василиск Команский», with the rank words left off. The day’s own line declines the name. The calendar’s index gives him the toponymic not of Amasea, where he was tried, but of Comana, where its own life has him beheaded on 22 May; the form is kept as the index prints it and the difference from this folder’s English name is named in the life. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form.

death.note: The two readings are kept and neither is chosen. doxologia.ro gave the reign of Diocletian and Maximian, 286 to 305, which is the interval this folder carried; days.pravoslavie.ru closes the line for 3 марта ст. ст. with «(ок. 308)» and opens its life «Святые мученики Евтропий, Клеоник и Василиск пострадали в городе Амасии Понтийской (Малая Азия) около 308 года». The «ок.» is that source’s own. The same life has Eutropius and Cleonicus crucified on the morning of 3 March and Basiliscus kept in prison and beheaded at Comana on 22 May, so the day of each death differs while the year does not; this corpus records years.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 3 марта ст. ст. — «Мчч. Евтропия , Клеоника и Василиска (ок. 308).»

feast.note: doxologia.ro prints him on 3 martie with Eutropius and Cleonicus; the life on the same site says his own memory is honoured on the day he died, «în douăzeci și două de zile ale lunii mai». Only the day the calendar prints is recorded here.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 3 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Vasilisc»

feast.note: saint.gr's own page for the three closes «Περισσότερα για τον Άγιο Βασιλίσκος μπορείτε να διαβάσετε στις 22 Μαΐου όπου επαναλαμβάνεται η μνήμη του» — more about him may be read on 22 May, where his memory is kept again (https://www.saint.gr/1728/saint.aspx, read 30 September 2026). That is the same second day doxologia gives him, already noted on this folder's Romanian row. The corpus keeps one feast to a church, so he renders on 3 March only.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 3ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιοι Ευτρόπιος, Κλεόνικος και Βασιλίσκος»

attestations.note: One page holds the three of them. It puts them at «την Αμάσεια του Πόντου» — Amasea of Pontus, where the corpus's own display names, taken from doxologia, say Cappadocia — makes them soldiers and kinsmen of St Theodore the Tiron, and sets them «κατά τους χρόνους του αυτοκράτορα Μαξιμιανού (286-305 μ.Χ.)» under the governor Asklepiodotos. It heads each of them «(; - 308)» and says «Στις 3 Μαρτίου του 308 μ.Χ., ο Ευτρόπιος και ο Κλεόνικος κοσμήθηκαν με τους στέφανους ... διά του σταυρικού τους θανάτου». That year lies outside the 286–305 interval this folder already holds from doxologia's reign of Maximian, and the two cannot both be right; the corpus's reading is left as it stands and saint.gr's year is recorded here. The page also has the Lord and the great-martyr Theodore appear to them twice, the idol of Artemis fall at Cleonicus's prayer, the boiling pitch burn the executioners instead of the martyrs, and the newly baptised onlookers beheaded. It prints four distichs, one for each man and one for the crucifixion, an apolytikion and a kontakion naming all three, and a second apolytikion which is the common of martyrs.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 16.03.2026 (3. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Евтропије, Клеоник и Василиск.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry. Its heading names all three men, so it is quoted whole by each of the three folders and the stored name form is this man’s own name out of it. Two differences from the pages already read for him are recorded rather than resolved. The Prologue has him beheaded with the sword in the same sentence as his companions’ crucifixion and says all three suffered in the year 308, where doxologia and saint.gr both leave him in prison and put his death later, on 22 May, which is the second day already noted on this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows. And 308 lies outside the interval this folder holds from doxologia, Maximian’s reign of 286 to 305, although saint.gr’s own life prints 308 for the other two. No day and no year was moved. **A SECOND DAY ON THIS CHURCH, ADDED 5 October 2026, AND IT SETTLES THE DISAGREEMENT THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE COULD ONLY RECORD.** The Prologue keeps him **again** on the Julian 22 May, in an entry of his own headed „Свети мученик Василиск.“ — Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 04.06.2026 (22. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Василиск.“ — and **that entry has him returned to prison after his companions died and beheaded long afterwards, which is doxologia’s and saint.gr’s reading and not the 3 March entry’s.** „Када ова последња двојица бише распети, и издахнуше 3. марта, Василиск би враћен поново у тамницу.“ **So the one book disagrees with itself across its own two days, and the later of the two agrees with the other two calendars.** `BRIEF.md` §4 allows a reader to write this note on a row that is already `venerated`, under `replace_venerated: true`, and **the row itself is copied back byte for byte** — same day, same month, same source, same year. **No second row was made and no day was moved**: one attestation row per church is the schema, this church’s row stays on the Julian 3 March, and he does not render on the 22 May. **He gains no new name form either**, the `sr` form «Василиск» being already stored off the 3 March heading and the 22 May heading printing the identical string — measured with `foldchk.py`, which returns `[('basiliscus-of-amasea', 'sr')]` and nothing else. **And the 22 May entry gives no year at all**, so the 308 of the 3 March entry is neither corroborated nor widened and `dates` is untouched. **New from the 22 May entry, and none of it is on any other page read for him**: that in the long imprisonment **he begged God with tears not to deny him a martyr’s death, and that the Lord Jesus Himself appeared to him, promised to grant it and sent him home to his village to greet his mother and his brothers**; that **the new governor Agrippa sent for him from the village, and that on the road from the village to Amasea the Lord worked great wonders through His martyr, so that many of the people believed in Christ**; that ordered to sacrifice to Apollo he answered **„Аполон значи губитељ!“**, Apollo means destroyer, and **crushed the idol to dust by fervent prayer and burned the temple with fire from heaven**; that **Agrippa put it down to magic and had him beheaded**, then **went mad, and in his madness went to the place of execution, found a little of the martyr’s blood in the dust, bound it under his belt and was made whole — and, coming to himself, was baptised**; and that **one Marin, a citizen of Komani — which was the name of the place of the beheading — raised a church on the martyr’s relics, where many sick found healing**. **Agrippa and Marin gain no folders and no rows**: no calendar read for this corpus keeps either, and by the coordinator’s third ruling nothing is minted for them. `types` untouched. No `locations`, although Amasea and Komani are both named.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Eutropie, Cleonic și Vasilisc

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contests received crowns of incorruption from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength they overcame their tormentors, and broke the strengthless daring of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ our God, save Thou our souls.

hymns.text: Τὸ τρίστοιχον ἄθροισμα, τῶν Ἀθλητῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, Εὐτρόπιον μέλψωμεν, σὺν Βασιλίσκω ὁμού, τὸν θεῖον Κλεόνικον οὗτοι γὰρ τῆς Τριάδος, τὸ ὑπέρθεον κράτος, ἄθλοις ὑπερφυέσιν, ὠμολόγησαν πάσιν ἡ πάντοτε πρεσβεύουσι, σώζεσθαι ἅπαντας.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε, on the page the three of them share. It names all three and is one text for the company, not three. Beside it the page prints an «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον» in the same tone, «Οἱ Μάρτυρές σου Κύριε», which is the common of martyrs and names nobody; the proper apolytikion and the kontakion are the two taken here.

english.text: Let us sing the threefold company of the contenders of Christ — Eutropius, together with Basiliscus, and the divine Cleonicus; for by contests beyond nature they confessed before all the supremely divine sovereignty of the Trinity, and they intercede at all times that all may be saved.

hymns.text: Ἁρμονίᾳ πίστεως συνδεδεμένοι, τοῦ ἐχθροῦ διέλυσαν, τάς παρατάξεις ἐμφανῶς, σύν Εὐτροπίῳ Κλεόνικος, καί Βασιλίσκος γενναίως ἀθλήσαντες.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον, on the page the three of them share. It names all three and is one text for the company.

english.text: Bound together in the harmony of faith, Cleonicus with Eutropius and Basiliscus, contending nobly, broke up openly the battle lines of the enemy.
